record.paper_title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions
record.original_question: How can experiments determine the sign of the real part of the eta-nucleus scattering length, rather than only its magnitude, so that a near-threshold eta-nucleus pole can be classified as a bound state or a virtual state? The problem requires high-accuracy measurements of the eta-nucleus amplitude both above threshold, where observables are sensitive to the magnitude of the real part, and below threshold through inelastic channels that couple significantly to the eta-nucleus channel.

evidence.quote: It is the sign of the real part that decides, whether the nearby pole we want to investigate refers to a bound state or a virtual state.

Thus any measurement above the η–nucleus threshold is sensitive only to the magnitude of the real part, but not to its sign; measurements above threshold are necessary to pin down the absolute values of the real and the imaginary part of the scattering length.

Since we know the sign of the imaginary part high accuracy measurements of the energy dependence of the η–nucleus amplitude above and below the eta threshold allows one to extract the sign of the real part of the scattering length [44].
But what does it mean to measure an amplitude below threshold? This can only work by identifying inelastic channels that show a significant coupling to the η–nucleus channel.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an eta meson interacting with a nucleus, characterized at low energies by a complex s-wave scattering length a = Re(a) + i Im(a). The near-threshold structure of the eta-nucleus amplitude may contain a pole; depending on the sign of Re(a), this pole corresponds either to a true bound state (negative Re(a) in the standard convention) or to a virtual (unbound) state. Observables for elastic eta-nucleus scattering at center-of-mass energies above the eta-nucleus threshold are sensitive to |Re(a)| and |Im(a)| but, because they depend only on |a|^2-like combinations near threshold, are insensitive to the sign of Re(a). The sign of Im(a) is fixed by unitarity.

Devise an experimentally realizable program of measurements that uniquely determines the sign of Re(a) for a given eta-nucleus system, thereby classifying the near-threshold pole as a bound state or a virtual state. Specifically:

(a) Identify what observables of the eta-nucleus amplitude must be measured above threshold to fix the magnitudes |Re(a)| and |Im(a)| with high accuracy.

(b) Identify a set of inelastic hadronic channels which couple strongly to the eta-nucleus channel and whose amplitudes, analytically continued below the eta-nucleus threshold, retain measurable sensitivity to the eta-nucleus scattering length, and explain how the energy dependence of these inelastic observables across the eta threshold (cusp/threshold behavior) can be used to extract the sign of Re(a).

(c) Provide an analytic framework (e.g., a coupled-channel or Flatté-type parametrization) showing rigorously that the combined above-threshold and below-threshold data determine the sign of Re(a) uniquely, and quantify the experimental precision required to distinguish a bound state from a virtual state for light nuclear targets (such as 3He and 4He) where existing theoretical predictions disagree on whether a bound state exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and theoretical work (2021–2024) continue to address the discrimination between near-threshold bound and virtual states in eta-nucleus systems via complex scattering length analyses, with calculations disagreeing on whether light nuclei (3He, 4He) support genuine eta-mesic bound states. No conclusive experimental determination of the sign of Re(a) for eta-light-nucleus systems has been established, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Search for η-mesic nuclei: a review of experimental and theoretical advances
status_evidence.snippet: Numerous calculations disagree especially for light nuclear systems with 3He and 4He. Some indicate binding whereas most don't.
status_evidence.claim: Determination of whether eta-light-nucleus bound states exist (equivalently the sign of Re(a)) remains experimentally and theoretically unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the nature of near-threshold bound and virtual states
status_evidence.snippet: General analytic expressions relating binding energy/half-width of an unstable bound state to the complex-valued scattering length.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2021) theoretical work still formulates the framework relating complex scattering length to bound vs virtual state classification, indicating the problem is actively studied.

status_evidence.title: Binding vs. scattering length: η in light nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Connection of the binding energy and width to the complex scattering length for s-states is relevant for searches of possible bound states.
status_evidence.claim: The sign-of-Re(a) question is the central unresolved issue distinguishing bound vs virtual eta-nucleus states.
